intro: Raesfeld is a small town in the Münsterland of North Rhine-Westphalia, near the Dutch border at Winterswijk. On the green of its village of Erle stands the Femeiche, an oak under which a Feme court sat until 1589, held up today by wooden props. Germany's dendrologists measured it at 12.45 metres round, and in 2021 it was named one of the country's national heritage trees. A reader sent us its photograph, taken at dusk.

trees.story:
Until 1589, a Feme court sat in judgement under this oak. The Erler Femeiche stands on the green of Erle, a village of Raesfeld on the edge of the Münsterland, and German sources call it the oldest and best-known court tree in Central Europe. In October 2021 it was named the twelfth of Germany's national heritage trees; the reader who sent us this photograph writes that it "has been the first national heritage tree of North Rhine-Westphalia since October 30, 2021."

Nobody agrees on its age. The newest findings cited on its Wikipedia page put it between 600 and 850 years, the German Dendrological Society's champion tree record estimates about 900, and older accounts reach 1,500. The reader gives it 1,000. Its size is less in doubt. The society measured the trunk at 12.45 metres round in August 2021.

The reader took the photograph at dusk, with the last blue in the sky and a lamp lighting the trunk from behind. The trunk has broken into separate pillars of old wood, green with moss, and they still hold up a crown in full leaf. Tall wooden props stand under the limbs, successors to ones first set there in 1892, and a round picket fence keeps visitors a few steps away.

Walk the path all the way round the fence to see each prop and pillar in turn.

question_meta: The Erler Femeiche at Raesfeld-Erle: the old court oak where a Feme court sat until 1589, its age, its girth, and how to find it.
question_answer: The Erler Femeiche stands on the village green at Erle, part of Raesfeld in North Rhine-Westphalia. It is free to visit at any hour; a fence keeps visitors a few metres from the trunk.
question_context: The Erler Femeiche is a pedunculate oak on the green of Erle, a village of Raesfeld on the edge of the Münsterland, a short drive from the Dutch border at Winterswijk. A Feme court sat under it until 1589, and German sources call it the oldest and best-known court tree in Central Europe. In October 2021 it was named the twelfth of Germany's national heritage trees. Its age is uncertain: the newest findings put it between 600 and 850 years, the German Dendrological Society estimates about 900, older accounts reach 1,500, and the reader who sent us its photograph gives 1,000. The society measured its trunk at 12.45 metres round in August 2021. The trunk has broken into separate pillars of old wood that still carry a crown in leaf, propped on wooden posts first set there in 1892 and since replaced. It stands inside a round picket fence and can be seen at any hour from the path that circles it.

faq.a: On the village green at Erle, part of Raesfeld in the Borken district of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany.

faq.q: How old is the Erler Femeiche?
faq.a: Estimates differ: 600 to 850 years by the newest findings, about 900 by the German Dendrological Society, and up to 1,500 in older accounts.

faq.q: Can I visit the Erler Femeiche?
faq.a: Yes, for free and at any hour. A fence keeps visitors a few metres from the trunk, and a path runs round it.
